title: CLAY COUNTY FAIR SCHEDULE
full_story:
The Clay County Fair will start tonight at 4 pm with the 33rd annual 4H BBQ at the REA building.  Menu is a Salt & Strings pork chop, green beans, cheesy potatoes, homemade desert and drink for $12, or $5 for a hot dog meal.  You can pre-purchase tickets from Clay County 4-H members, or you can stop by the extension office at 210 S Church St., Louisville, or you can buy tickets at the door.

Gates will then open at 5:30 for the Crain Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  Cost to enter the rodeo is $15, those 5 and under get in for free, pre show tickets are available from Young Leaders and are $12.  Mutton busting will be available for $10 with only 30 spots available for children under 80 lbs.  Carnival rides will also open tonight.  The Clay County Health Department Hospice Volunteers will be at the Clay County Fair selling raffle tickets for their annual Hospice Volunteer Meat Raffle fundraiser.  Two lucky winners will receive a $250 or $200 gift certificate to their choice of either Blair’s Slaughtering & Processing or Salt & Strings Butchery both located in Louisville.  Raffle tickets are $10 each and will be available before the evening fair events tonight, and again Monday through Friday.  All proceeds benefit the Clay County Health Department Hospice Volunteer Program, which provides comfort and support to local hospice patients and their families during end-of-life care.

Tomorrow morning starts at 8 am with the poultry and rabbit check in.  The poultry show is at 9 am followed by the 4H and JR Rabbit Show.  All livestock should be on the fairgrounds by 3 pm.  There will also be a mandatory meeting for all livestock exhibitors and vet papers check at 3 pm.  After the meeting livestock weigh in will begin, and the night ends at 7 pm with the open sheep show.

Sunday, will have the JR Sheep show at 11 am and JR Goat show at Noon.  Registration for the kids pedal tractor pull at 1 pm next to the Merchants building, and the kids pull is at 2 pm, hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The 4H Horse show and JR Horse show is at 2 pm.  The Clay County 4H Federation will have yard games from 5 to 7 pm.  The Clay County Ministerial Alliance program is from 5:30 to 7 pm and there will be a greased pig contest at 7 pm sponsored by UPI Fairfield.

On Monday, the fair will kick into high gear with the 4H Beef Show at 8 am followed by the JR Beef Show, AITC Activities will be in the Farm Bureau building from 2 to 4 pm.  Then at 5 pm it’s the Mini Livestock Show for those 4 to 8 years of age hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The night ends with the Little Miss Pageant at 7:30 pm admission is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 19 young ladies vying for the title held by Izzabella Brinkley.

Tuesday will be Nutrien Ag Solutions Day at the fair with giveaways and activities throughout the day.  At 8 am is the 4H Swine show and Open Beef Show, followed by the Sheep Show at 1 pm and the 4H Goat Show at 2:30 pm.  Then at 5 pm will be the Master Showmanship Contest, sponsored by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  On the stage at 7:30 pm will be the Junior Miss Clay County Fair Pageant and Queen pie auction.  Admission to the Junior Miss pageant is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 10 contestants, Halle Patridge is the current JR Miss.

Wednesday will start at 8 am with the JR Swine Show followed by the Open Goat Show.  DaS zle Dance and Tumble will perform at 5 pm, admission is free, and the 4H Livestock Auction will begin at 6:30pm.

Thursday opens at 8 am with the Open Dairy Show, then at 5 pm Joni’s Power & Grace Tumbling will be in the REA building, admission is free.  The Lickity Split and Legally Sheila concert will be on the stage 7 pm.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, July 31st at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

title: STATUS HEARING HELD
full_story:
A status hearing took place Thursday morning for Dylan M. Jones, the Olney man accused of killing 52-year-old John D. Jones Jr. and 73-year-old Deborah J. Jones, in Richland County.

According to court documents, 25-year-old Dylan M. Jones is facing 4 counts of Murder with the Intent to Kill or Injure and 2 counts of Murder with the Strong Probability to Kill or Injure.  Police believe Dylan Jones struck John Jones Jr. in the head with a sharp object.  They also believe he stabbed Deborah Jones to death.

During the status hearing Court officials focused on two-key factors; Jones’ medication and his competency evaluation to see if he is “fit” to stand trial.  The defense attorney advised the Court that they are “trying to find a fitness evaluator who can perform an evaluation sooner than mid to late August”, according to court documents.

title: TOP LPN PROGRAMS
full_story:
The Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Nursing Program earned statewide recognition for excellence in nursing education.

PracticalNursing.org ranked Olney Central College and Wabash Valley College No. 1 and No. 2, respectively, in its 2026 list of the Top Licensed Practical Nursing (LPN) programs in Illinois.

A trusted source for nursing education information, licensure guidance and career resources, PracticalNursing.org provides data-driven rankings to help prospective students identify quality nursing programs.

The annual rankings recognize programs that demonstrate excellence in preparing the next generation of nurses.  Both OCC and WVC were singled out for the honor because of their flexible exit pathways and hands-on training, which open expanded opportunities for nursing students across Southeastern Illinois.

Among the program’s defining features is its distinctive summer “exit” course, offered between the first and second years of the Associate Degree Nursing Program.  This option allows students to earn LPN licensure while continuing their progress toward an associate degree and eligibility for registered nurse licensure.

“Our Practical Nursing Program is unique as a ladder program within the state of Illinois,” said Dr. Alanni Frederick, IECC Dean of Health Professions.  “We are able to educate our students concurrently and get them into the workforce faster.  Due to the unique setup and strong preparation, our students are able to be successful both in licensure and at the bedside.  Examining board scores, graduate feedback and employer evaluations allows us to ensure our program is prepared to educate at the highest level.”

The rankings were based on several factors, including accreditation, program quality and academic excellence, affordability, learning flexibility and admission rates.

“IECC is committed to ensuring that local students receive a strong education to give back to our local communities,” Frederick said.  “With a program like nursing, our students learn how to care in our community and for our community.”

For Frederick, the top rankings underscore the impact of the IECC Nursing Program and the opportunities it provides for students to build successful healthcare careers.

“We want our prospective students to know that a high-quality education is available in our own backyard,” she added.  “If you have ever thought about healthcare, now is the time.”

To learn more about the IECC Nursing Program, visit www.iecc.edu/nursing.  Additional information regarding the PracticalNursing.org rankings is available at: https://www.practicalnursing.org/lpn-programs/illinois.

title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County on August 11th.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Speakers will be Liesl Wingert from the SIU School of Medicine, Shelly Kuhns, with Gentle Care Consultants, Andy Greer with the Gateway Foundation, Clay County States Attorney Phil Givens, and Clay County Sheriff’s Sgt Elam Lewis.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are pending.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

title: GRAND AMERICAN
full_story:
Sparta’s World Shooting and Recreational Complex will host the Amateur Trapshooting Association’s 127th Grand American championships this summer.

The Grand American will take place starting Wednesday and end on August 8th.  More than 5,000 competitors and spectators from all over the world will take part in and attend the competition.

The World Shooting Complex has hosted the Grand American every year since 2006.

“Hosting the Grand American is a tremendous point of pride for Illinois, and IDNR is grateful for its long-standing partnership with the Amateur Trapshooting Association,” said IDNR interim Director Renee Snow.  “IDNR is committed to supporting this event and ensuring the World Shooting and Recreational Complex remains a national destination for shooting sports and outdoor recreation.”

For a full schedule of events and information about the Amateur Trapshooting Association, visit the association’s website.  For more information about recreation, dining, and event-hosting capabilities at the facility, visit the World Shooting and Recreational Complex’s website.

title: LAKE LAND STEM NIGHT
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting its first-ever community STEM night at the Effingham Technology Center, giving community members of all ages the chance to enjoy hands-on activities with high-tech educational equipment.

The Lake Land College community STEM night will be held on Wednesday, August 5th from 5-7 pm.  The event will focus on video game development, with in-depth instruction and demonstration led by Lake Land College staff.

All attendees will also get to practice coding and design their very own video games.  Attendees can also bring a flash drive to save and take home their games.

The event will take place in the Lake Land College Innovation Center on the first floor of the Effingham Technology Center.  Registration is not required to attend the event.

For more information about Lake Land College community STEM night, contact Innovation Center Assistant Tiffany Maillet-Gibson at 217-234-5328 or [email protected].

title: SUTHERLAND APPEAL REJECTED
full_story:
71-year-old Cecil Sutherland has had two jury trials and was sentenced to death twice in the rape and murder of Amy Schulz 39 years ago.  Despite that, Sutherland continues to appeal his conviction, claiming ineffective assistance of counsel.  His latest appeal was rejected last week by the justices of the Fifth District Court of Appeals in Mt. Vernon.

Specifically, Sutherland asked the justices to reverse the second stage dismissal of his appeal and remand for a third stage evidentiary hearing on his ineffective assistance of counsel claims.  The appellate court said no, rejecting this latest bid for relief.

On the evening of July 1, 1987, Amy Schulz left her Kell home in rural Marion County to search for her brother’s dog that had run away.  Her nude body was found the following day near an oil lease road in Jefferson County.  Several months after the crime, police were contacted by law enforcement authorities at Glacier National Park in Montana where Sutherland had been arrested for shooting at park rangers.  The tread on the right front tire of Sutherland’s car matched tracks left at the scene of the murder.  Dog hairs found on Amy’s clothing matched Sutherland’s black Labrador and fibers from the carpet and upholstery in his car matched those found on Amy’s clothing.

In 1989, a Jefferson County jury convicted Sutherland of murder and rape, resulting in the imposition of the death penalty.  Sutherland appealed, claiming ineffective assistance of counsel.  While the appellate court rejected the appeal, the Illinois Supreme Court reversed the decision and ordered a new trial.  Following a five-week trial in 2004, Sutherland was once again convicted of murder and rape and sentenced to death.  In 2011, Governor Patrick Quinn commuted Sutherland’s death sentence.

In 1990, Amy’s father, Dennis Schulz helped establish the Amy Schulz Child Advocacy Center in Mt. Vernon.  The Amy Center serves seven Southern Illinois counties, including, Clay, Wayne, Hamilton, Clinton, Jefferson, Marion and Washington.

title: DU QUOIN STATE FAIR ONLINE REGISTRATION
full_story:
The Du Quoin State Fair announced that Livestock, Equine, and Home Show exhibitor registration has moved online using ShoWorks.  This new system, and the Premium Books, are now available on the Du Quoin State Fair website.

The Du Quoin State Fair staff, along with show superintendents and youth advisors, have been working behind the scenes for months to convert the paper-entry system into a new digital platform.

“We are excited to bring our registration process into the 21st century with this powerful tool,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture.  “Our priority is to make the process more efficient for our exhibitors.”

“Online registration has become the standard across the industry, and ShoWorks allows us to meet those expectations,” said Luke Davison, Manager of the Du Quoin State Fair.  “Most exhibitors are already familiar with systems like this, making the transition seamless while giving us a more efficient and secure way to manage entries.”

A step-by-step tutorial on the Competitive Events page will help guide you every step of the way.  Exhibitors can call the Competitive Events office at 618-542-1509 or 618-542-1525.  The Competitive Events office is open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4 pm.

The Du Quoin State Fair runs from August 28th through September 7th.  To learn more, visit dsf.illinois.gov/.

title: HOUSE OK’S $12B SUPPORT
full_story:
The US House advanced a reconciliation package including $12 billion for farmer support, but bill passage in the Senate will likely be a challenge.

The House passed the $95 billion budget measure, or “reconciliation 3.0,” by a vote of 216-214.  The legislation provides funds for the Iran war, new election laws and up to $12 billion to help struggling farmers.  The bill also includes the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and photo ID to vote in federal elections.

The legislation is now in the Senate’s court, with senators scheduled for their August recess in two weeks.  House members already left for their August recess for five weeks to campaign for the midterm elections.

Illinois Farm Bureau applauded the House’s action to provide much-needed economic relief to struggling farms across the country.

“The farm economy has faced significant challenges for several years, and conditions are expected to worsen for the sixth year as producers continue to face high production costs, low commodity prices and shrinking margins,” IFB President Philip Nelson said.

“These ongoing pressures continue to place tremendous strain on farm families, underscoring the need for long-term policy solutions that deliver certainty, stability and meaningful relief.  We urge the US Senate to swiftly pass economic relief and advance critical priorities such as year-round E15 and a five-year farm bill before the August recess to provide the support and predictability farmers need.”

Fiscal hawks have criticized the budget blueprint for its lack of pay-fors, and with Senator Mitch McConnell’s, medical-related absence, it’s unclear if the Senate has enough Republican votes to advance the budget framework.

title: SEPARATE ILLINOIS
full_story:
A growing movement to separate parts of Illinois from Cook County is gaining momentum, with nearly one-third of the state’s 107 counties voting to explore the idea of creating a new state.

County boards in those areas have approved non-binding ballot measures that will allow voters to weigh in on the proposal later this year.

While the referendums would not change state boundaries, supporters say they are intended to gauge public support for the idea.

The proposal stems from concerns among some residents who believe their political priorities are overshadowed by the influence of Cook County and the Chicago metropolitan area.

If the effort does not ultimately lead to changes, one local political analyst believes some residents may choose to leave Illinois altogether.

“States like California, Illinois, New Jersey and New York are seeing a lot of residents leaving.  They have a negative outgrowth, and a lot of these people are going to other states,” said John A. Logan College Political Science and Sociology instructor Matt Lees.

Supporters of the proposal to split Illinois say additional counties are expected to place similar non-binding referendum questions on the ballot this fall, allowing more voters to voice their opinions on the issue.

Any effort to create a new state would require approval from both the Illinois General Assembly and US Congress, making it a lengthy and complex process.
